title: CHGR shared identifier definitions
description: Layer 2 shape-only identifier definitions for the CHGR schema family (Phase 143E, CHGR-001 v1.0 Sec.9). record_identity is a generic, family-prefixed shape (mirrors src/pcae/schema_resources/cltr_cutover/shared/identity.schema.json's own record_identity convention, independently defined here per CHGR-001 Sec.16/Sec.19.1's no-composition-across-families rule) used by every CHGR artifact type's own envelope.record_id -- never a filesystem path, date, or agent identity, and never encoding a template/schema version (CHGR-REQ-078, CHGR-REQ-079). A well-formed identifier never itself establishes authority (CHGR-REQ-080).

record_identity.description: Generic CHGR record_id shape: lowercase-only, family-prefixed by convention (e.g. 'chgr-<32-hex-uuid4>' for a HumanGovernanceRecord, 'chgrconf-<32-hex-uuid4>' for a HumanConfirmationEvidence, 'chgrprov-...' for GovernanceRecordProvenance, 'chgrintg-...' for GovernanceRecordIntegrity, 'chgrevt-...' for a GovernanceRecordLifecycleEvent), 8-128 characters total, charset [a-z0-9-] after the leading letter. This shared shape definition does not itself enforce a specific per-family prefix; each records/*.schema.json file may further restrict via its own pattern if it needs to. Self-contained; independent of file path, branch, or remote (CHGR-REQ-078). Never reused or reassigned once assigned to a published HumanGovernanceRecord, even after revocation (CHGR-REQ-077).

template_identity.description: Stable Decision Template identifier (CHGR-REQ-049), e.g. 'gac001-sec9-stage6'. Lowercase-only, 3-64 characters, charset [a-z0-9_-] after the leading letter. A distinct namespace from record_identity: a template is a governed definition, never a Human Governance Act instance.

template_version.description: Decision Template semver (MAJOR.MINOR), immutable once referenced by any published record.

evidence_kind.description: L0: 'typed_confirmation_only' (evidence of deliberate intent only, no identity binding beyond whoever operated the session). L1: 'os_authenticated_user' (adds OS/session user-identity binding). No L2-L5 value is defined here -- deliberate absence is the mechanism preventing an overclaim (CHGR-REQ-103); a record claiming L2+ assurance without a matching evidence_kind fails ASSURANCE_OVERCLAIM at verification, never at this schema layer.

identifier.description: The identity evidence value at the achieved level (e.g. an OS username at L1), or the literal string 'unavailable' at L0 where no identity beyond session origin exists to disclose.

captured_at.description: When this identity evidence was captured, honestly reflecting the confirmation event time -- never backdated or estimated.

decision_maker_identity_evidence.description: Identity evidence honestly scoped to the achieved assurance level (CHGR-001 Sec.9). Never represented as cryptographic identity this increment.
